predictions.title: Open-source serving stacks ship signed-checkpoint loading as default by Q4 2026
predictions.body: By Q4 2026 the Tuesday serving-tier and local-LLM-stack adoption of the DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft joint signed-checkpoint reference implementation forces the open-source inference-serving cohort — vLLM, SGLang, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and Ray Serve — to ship signature-verified model-checkpoint loading as the documented default load path at the serving tier rather than as an opt-in feature. The Tuesday catalysts are concrete and mutually reinforcing: vLLM v0.11.3 ships a Tuesday point release adding a Sigstore-or-cosign-compatible signature-verified model-checkpoint loader and becomes the first open-source serving stack to ship the signed-checkpoint primitive at the serving tier; Unsloth ships the same primitive at the local-LLM fine-tuning stack tier on the same day, the first local-LLM stack to do so ahead of the framework cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment target; the Cloudflare Infire production-deployment note reports the new loader plus the tensor-parallel disaggregated-prefill mode close the L40S edge-tier latency gap to a 1.18x Infire advantage (down from 1.25x at the v0.11.2 Monday checkpoint) with a parity-window targeted at v0.11.4 in late-May; the Yotta Labs canonical benchmark refresh places vLLM v0.11.3 at approximately 16,580 tok/s on the shared-prefix workload versus 18,140 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.6, narrowing the throughput gap to 9.4 percent from 11.3 percent Monday; and the Tuesday DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft joint follow-up preprint (arxiv 2605.06712) extends the Monday signed-checkpoint format to cover the inference-routing tier and explicitly anchors the runtime-verifier integration pattern to vLLM, SGLang, TGI, and TensorRT-LLM as the reference serving stacks. The structural force is that once one production-tier serving stack ships signature-verified loading on the same day a leading local-LLM fine-tuning stack ships the matching primitive, and the runtime-verifier preprint anchors the cohort with named reference implementations, the remaining serving-tier maintainers cannot leave unsigned checkpoint loading as the documented default while the cyber-eval reciprocity attestation field schema and the CISA KEV cadence treat signed-load posture as paired procurement-eligibility evidence; the convergence of the vLLM-SGLang throughput gap to single digits removes the last performance argument for postponing the change. The most likely shape is the signed-checkpoint loader becoming the default load path in the next minor release of SGLang RadixArk, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, Triton Inference Server, and Ray Serve, with an explicit unsigned-load opt-out flag for sandboxed test fixtures and reproduction harnesses; sovereign-cloud and FedRAMP-Moderate serving tenants adopt the loader first because the Indo-Pacific eleven-jurisdiction cohort plus the AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex agent-registry public-preview interop already exposes signed-load posture as a tenant-policy field. Bear case is that one serving stack forks the loader contract or ships a sandbox-only mitigation; absent that, Q4 2026 lands signature-verified model-checkpoint loading as the documented default at the serving tier across the open-source cohort.

reasoning.because: Tuesday vLLM v0.11.3 + Unsloth ship signed-checkpoint loader same day; runtime-verifier preprint.
reasoning.given: vLLM-SGLang throughput gap narrows to 9.4% and reciprocity attestation needs signed-load evidence.
reasoning.so_that: SGLang, TGI, TensorRT-LLM, Triton, and Ray Serve ship signature-verified loading as the documented default load path.
reasoning.landing: By Q4 2026; open-source serving cohort; sovereign-cloud tenants first.
reasoning.plain_language: AI servers will soon refuse to load model files unless they are digitally signed, like apps on a phone.

predictions.summary: vLLM v0.11.3 ships a Tuesday signed-checkpoint loader as the first open-source serving stack; Unsloth ships the matching primitive at the local-LLM tier the same day. By Q4 2026 signature-verified checkpoint loading lands as the default load path across the open-source serving cohort.

predictions.title: SEC Corp Fin publishes AI-accelerator S-1 staff guidance by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the Tuesday SEC Division of Corporation Finance confidential-submission acknowledgement to Tenstorrent — formally opening the JOBS Act EGC 30-60 day review window with an early-August public-filing target intact per Jim Keller's Monday investor-relations note, with the May 8 SEC Corp Fin sample comment letter on AI-services-revenue measurement basis plus the Cerebras CBRS S-1 single-counterparty risk-factor exhibit pattern explicitly named in the Tuesday submission-acknowledgement working notes as the operative precedent set — combined with SambaNova Systems' Tuesday roster update adding Barclays Capital as the fifth joint lead bookrunner alongside J.P. Morgan, Citi, Goldman Sachs, and Wells Fargo Securities (the late-June confidential-submission target unchanged), Groq's process running 30-60 days behind pending the sovereign-cloud Saudi Arabia commitment closure with the Saudi Public Investment Fund contingent secondary discussion now referencing the Cerebras post-IPO valuation as the operative reference comparable, and the Mag-7 print-cycle preview cohort (Bernstein, Wells Fargo Securities, Evercore ISI, Citi Research) lifting the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability to 72 percent citing the post-IPO Cerebras CBRS valuation as the operative AI-accelerator-revenue multiple comparable, force the SEC Corp Fin precedent set to crystallize from an ad-hoc per-S-1 comment-letter pattern into a published staff guidance bundle covering AI-accelerator IPO disclosure shape across the AI-services-revenue measurement basis plus single-counterparty concentration risk-factor disclosure plus hyperscaler-anchor warrant-equity counterparty disclosure axes. The forcing function is that when one staff comment letter plus one operative S-1 risk-factor exhibit pattern get formally named in submission-acknowledgement working notes as the precedent set for three back-to-back AI-accelerator IPO confidential submissions inside a 90-day window (Cerebras priced late April, Tenstorrent in formal review Tuesday, SambaNova on a late-June submission target, Groq trailing 30-60 days behind), the Corp Fin staff cannot manage the cohort review load through one-off comment letters alone — the precedent set must move to a standardized staff-guidance shape (a Staff Legal Bulletin, a topical disclosure release, or a Corp Fin compliance and disclosure interpretation update) so that issuer counsel, audit committee chairs, and underwriter due-diligence teams have a citable Corp Fin position on AI-services revenue recognition basis, single-counterparty concentration disclosure threshold, and hyperscaler-warrant-equity counterparty footnote shape before each new AI-accelerator S-1 enters the review queue. The most likely shape is a Corp Fin Staff Legal Bulletin or topical AI-accelerator IPO disclosure release issued before the SambaNova S-1 public filing window, covering AI-services-revenue measurement basis (entailing recognition timing for usage-tiered hyperscaler contracts plus committed-purchase-order treatment), single-counterparty concentration risk-factor disclosure (entailing the Cerebras CBRS exhibit pattern as the working baseline plus a quantitative concentration-threshold trigger), and hyperscaler-anchor warrant-equity counterparty disclosure (entailing the Anthropic and OpenAI structured-equity JV template as the cross-vendor reference). Sovereign-wealth-fund and hyperscaler counterparty disclosure adopt first because the Saudi PIF Groq discussion plus the Apple Cerebras supply agreement plus the Anthropic-Blackstone JV template each surface counterparty-disclosure questions the existing Cerebras CBRS S-1 exhibit only partially answers. Bear case is that the SEC Corp Fin staff defers a published bundle in favor of continuing the per-S-1 comment-letter pattern citing the existing precedent set; absent that, Q3 2026 lands a standardized Corp Fin AI-accelerator IPO disclosure staff guidance release before SambaNova hits the public-filing window.

reasoning.because: Tuesday Corp Fin opens Tenstorrent 30-60 day review; CBRS S-1 is the named operative precedent.
reasoning.given: May 8 sample comment letter + Cerebras CBRS single-counterparty exhibit named in working notes.
reasoning.so_that: Corp Fin publishes a standardized AI-accelerator S-1 staff guidance bundle on revenue + counterparty disclosure.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; staff legal bulletin or disclosure release before SambaNova S-1 GA.
reasoning.plain_language: The SEC just opened Tenstorrent IPO review using Cerebras S-1 as template; soon they will publish that template as official rules.

predictions.summary: SEC Corp Fin issues Tenstorrent a Tuesday confidential-submission acknowledgement opening the 30-60 day review; working notes name the May 8 sample comment letter + Cerebras CBRS S-1 as the operative precedent. By Q3 2026 Corp Fin publishes standardized AI-accelerator S-1 staff guidance.

predictions.title: Cyber-eval reciprocity attestation lands as agent-registry GA default by Q3 2026
predictions.body: By Q3 2026 the Indo-Pacific cyber-eval reciprocity attestation field schema — first wired into the Sunday three-hyperscaler registry interop matrix as a tenant-policy field set, then carried into Tuesday's OpenAI ChatGPT Enterprise per-org agent registry GA cohort for Singapore-cloud and Japan-cloud tenants on Microsoft Azure plus AWS Bedrock plus Google Cloud Vertex simultaneously — becomes the de facto cross-vendor agent-registry GA-tier tenant-policy default across the four-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix (OpenAI Codex CLI plus Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 plus Mistral Workflows plus Microsoft Azure AI Foundry plus Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center). The trigger is the simultaneous Tuesday landing of three structurally complementary moves: the Indo-Pacific reciprocity perimeter crosses to eleven named jurisdictions with the first formal Latin American extension (Thailand entry note plus Chile and Mexico exploratory observers under the OECD GENAI working-group baseline), giving the schema cross-hemispheric reach; OpenAI cites the May 8 Singapore IMDA plus Japan AISI memorandum plus the Sunday-shipped South Korea PIPC plus New Zealand GCSB reciprocity-attestation fields as the operative tenant-policy schema for the per-org agent registry GA cohort, anchoring the schema at the hyperscaler agent-registry GA tier rather than the public-preview tier; and the four-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix completes in pre-GA form with Google Cloud Vertex AI Agent Governance Center managed interop joining the Codex CLI plus Claude Code 3.0 plus Mistral Workflows plus Azure AI Foundry pre-GA cohort, demonstrating that the reciprocity-attestation field schema is the only tenant-policy primitive every vendor in the matrix already speaks. The structural force is procurement-driven rather than standards-driven: when the schema is the only cross-vendor primitive shared across a four-vendor interop matrix AND the hyperscaler GA-tier tenant-policy schema AND the eleven-jurisdiction allied policy regime AND the Tuesday Verifiable Cross-Hemispheric Composition arxiv 2605.06584 paper as the citable formal-verification anchor, the cohort-completion gravity locks the schema as the default at the agent-registry GA tier — any vendor shipping a GA registry on a hyperscaler sovereign-cloud tenancy without the attestation fields fails procurement gating from the Indo-Pacific cohort. The landing shape: by Q3 2026 at least one additional frontier-lab agent registry (Mistral or Anthropic) ships GA on the same Singapore plus Japan sovereign-cloud tenancy citing the same reciprocity-attestation field schema, and at least one hyperscaler publishes a Skill Catalog or Agent Governance Center GA tier requiring the attestation fields as the default tenant-policy schema for new agent-registry provisioning on Indo-Pacific sovereign-cloud regions. The US recognition gap remains the structural pressure point — the schema lands as a cross-vendor GA default regardless of whether the FMRB executive order signs first, because the procurement-enforcement pathway is already cross-vendor and cross-hyperscaler on the eleven-jurisdiction perimeter. Bear case is that the FMRB executive order ships a US-side mandatory schema variant that fragments the field set before the cross-vendor GA default locks; absent that, Q3 2026 lands the schema as the operative agent-registry GA tenant-policy default across the four-vendor matrix on Indo-Pacific sovereign-cloud tenants.

reasoning.because: Tuesday OpenAI per-org agent registry GA cites reciprocity-attestation fields as tenant schema.
reasoning.given: It is the only cross-vendor primitive shared by the four-vendor matrix and 11-jurisdiction cohort.
reasoning.so_that: At least one more frontier-lab registry + one hyperscaler Skill Catalog ship GA defaulting to the schema.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; Indo-Pacific sovereign-cloud tenants; agent-registry GA tier.
reasoning.plain_language: Allied countries agreed on a list of AI safety checks; vendors now use it for enterprise setups, and it will be the default by autumn.

predictions.summary: OpenAI's Tuesday per-org agent registry GA on Singapore and Japan sovereign-cloud cites the Indo-Pacific reciprocity-attestation fields as the tenant-policy schema; the four-vendor interop matrix shares no other primitive. By Q3 2026 the schema becomes the cross-vendor agent-registry GA default.
